headline: Mileage jumps are where injuries start
insight: In weeks when an athlete ran more than 30% above their own 4-week average (load ratio over 1.3), an injury began within the next two weeks 11.3% of the time (6 of 53 weeks). In steady weeks (0.8 to 1.3) it was 1.4% (16 of 1,182).
action: Flag any planned week above 1.3 before it happens, especially for underclassmen and athletes coming back from time off.

headline: Comebacks are ramping too fast
insight: All three athletes hurt twice this season (Silas Mercado, Paige Juarez, Simon Hollis) got hurt the second time within two weeks of a comeback week at 1.5 or higher. The same pattern is showing now: Rafael Flores, Paige Juarez and Willa Moreno each ran above 1.6 the week of Oct 12, and Lucia Sorensen is at 1.6 this week, all within three weeks of returning.
action: Use a written, graded return-to-run plan with your athletic trainer and keep returning athletes under 1.3 until they are back to full volume.

headline: Three warning signs line up for Lucia
insight: Her load ratio is 1.6 this week (39.2 miles) right after missing time with a hamstring strain. In the Oct 20 5 x 1K her heart rate averaged 202 bpm, up from 195 in the Sep 15 6 x 1K at a similar pace, and her heart rate dropped only 18.5 bpm in the first 60 seconds of rest, about half the team median of 36.2.
action: Check sleep, illness and fueling, and hold her to easy running until her workout heart rate settles before the championship.

headline: Higher heart rate at the same pace
insight: Both ran the Oct 20 5 x 1K at their usual pace, but with heart rate about 7 to 8 bpm higher than in the Sep 15 6 x 1K (Adrian 206 vs 199, Ruby 195 vs 187), and recovered only 18 to 19 bpm between reps. Neither had a mileage spike, which points to something outside running, such as illness, sleep or school stress.
action: Do a quick check-in with both before the next workout.

headline: Not every injury follows a spike
insight: Sofia Brennan's tibial bone stress injury (Oct 21) came after steady training, with load ratios of 1.02 and 0.81 in the two weeks before. Bone stress injuries in teenage runners often involve factors beyond mileage, such as sleep, nutrition and injury history.
action: Have her return plan come from your sports medicine staff or her physician, not the standard comeback progression.

headline: Speed is up but the 5K is flat
insight: Compared with 2025 XC, Rowan is 10.8 s faster for 1 mile, 23.4 s faster for 1.5 miles and 25.8 s faster for 2 miles, but only 3.0 s faster for the 5K. The fitness gain is not carrying through the last mile.
action: Add threshold volume and extend his long run gradually, then watch his final-mile splits in the next race.

headline: Returners are clearly faster
insight: The 45 athletes with a 2025 XC 5K are a median 35.1 s faster this season, and 14 of 62 athletes have already reached their 5K goal.
action: Use the goal gap column on the Performance tab to set championship targets.
